note: RE-MODEL against the v1.0.0 paper baseline (decklist sha 88bffd9b…). The previous engine.json was written against the pre-baseline list and failed validate-engine with 13 errors: ten cards named in stages that have left the 99, one line routed through Bontu's Monument, and nine arrivals placed nowhere. Where the old reading still holds it is kept. Three inputs are new since it was written: checker-passed stack 010, the deck's first logged game (log.jsonl 001 + log_annotations.json), and an amended goldfish declaration that adds a third leg to THE GO-WIDE KILL.
thesis: Edgar's eminence mints a free body every time you cast a Vampire and the doublers turn one mint into eight, so this deck wins by CASTING cheap creatures into a payoff that bills all three seats at once — and after the v1.0.0 baseline it does that by drawing more chances at the piece rather than by going and finding it.

stages.label: WHAT PAYS FOR THE NEXT CAST
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-six land copies across 32 entries (Swamp x4, Plains x2) — copies is what a shuffler sees — plus six accelerants. deck-audit reads mana-base 36 against the aggro band 34-36, mana-sources 42 against Burgess's 40, and taplands 3 unconditional (twelve more are conditional or pay life): all three AT target. The job is narrow. This engine does not want a big turn, it wants a cheap Vampire cast EVERY turn, because that cast is the trigger everything else waits on. What is not at target is colour: deck-audit puts the deck 6 sources short on its worst colour, black at 30 of a 36 Karsten target and red at 18 of 22, while white is exactly 22 of 22 — and black carries 45 of the deck's 83 pips (deck-facts). One of those 30 black sources is restricted (below). The baseline is where the pressure comes from: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth made every land a Swamp and left with it. Two cards here are not mana in the ordinary sense. Master of Dark Rites taps and sacrifices another creature for {B}{B}{B} spendable only on Vampire, Cleric and Demon spells — deck-facts flags it `spells_only`, so it cannot pay a coloured activated ability, though it does pay part of Edgar's own cost. Herald's Horn discounts Vampire creature spells by {1}, and a generic reduction cannot pay a coloured pip (CR 601.2f): eleven of the thirteen Vampires in the ignition leg carry no generic component at all — only Blood Artist {1}{B} and Charismatic Conqueror {1}{W} do — so the discount misses the exact cards this engine casts. The hardest cast in the 99 is Bloodletter of Aclazotz at {1}{B}{B}{B}, the only cost here with three black pips.
cards: Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid

stages.label: TWO LEGS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS FREE
stages.what_it_does: Edgar Markov's eminence reads 'whenever you cast another Vampire spell, if Edgar is in the command zone or on the battlefield, create a 1/1 black Vampire creature token' — live from the command zone in 100% of games and never drawn. Stack 010 re-proves it with Edgar having NEVER entered the battlefield. The second leg has to be drawn: a Vampire spell must actually be cast, and every checker-passed proof of the go-wide kill (002, 008, 009, 010) opens by casting a two-mana Vampire — read off each scenario's stack[] rather than its board: Gifted Aetherborn in 002, 008 and 010, and Cordial Vampire in 009. Cordial Vampire is on 002's board, which records that it never triggers, nothing having died. goldfish_targets now declares that leg (the thirteen Vampires at mana value 2 or less): 63.9% of opening sevens, 92.3% assembled, 84.8% by turn six, mean turn 2.12. Declaring it took THE GO-WIDE KILL from 0.531 to 0.491 assembled; the payoff split took it to 0.445, 0.285 by turn six, mean 5.043 — the kill did not get worse, the measurement twice stopped omitting something. Five of the thirteen are filed here because casting them is the whole of what they do; the other eight sit in four other stages doing a second job — four in wincon, two in output, Charismatic Conqueror in conversion and Master of Dark Rites in mana, and the 84.8% is measured across all thirteen, not across these five. Two cards that look like they belong and do not: Corpse Knight is a Zombie Knight and Witty Roastmaster a Devil Citizen, so casting either fires nothing. What switches this off is not removal — destruction and exile route Edgar to the command zone, where eminence already works. It is an ability-stripping aura, a control-change effect, a static tax, or a hand with no Vampire in it.

stages.label: THE REFUEL, AND TWO SEARCHES THAT COST A TURN
stages.what_it_does: What the engine eats is CASTS, so fuel is whatever keeps another cheap Vampire in hand. The declared draw component is seven cards — Caretaker's Talent, Welcoming Vampire, Preacher of the Schism, Night's Whisper, Champion of Dusk, Skullclamp, Pact of the Serpent — at 41.2% of opening sevens, 73.3% assembled, 62.1% by turn six, mean turn 2.855. It is priced in the two resources this deck banks: life (Champion of Dusk and Pact of the Serpent draw X and lose X; Night's Whisper is 2) and bodies (Skullclamp turns a minted 1/1 into two cards). Nothing here touches a graveyard. The baseline changed this stage's character rather than its size. Demonic Tutor and Diabolic Intent left; Forerunner of the Legion arrived. Both departures put a card INTO YOUR HAND; both survivors put it on TOP of the library, and one of the two can only find a Vampire. Every search now costs a turn — true of the cards, and NOT what the model measures: goldfish.py's _TUTOR_RE is the literal phrase 'search your library for a card', which Forerunner's 'search your library for a Vampire card' does not match, so it is not modelled as a tutor at all. The 7.5-point assisted gap on the go-wide kill (0.445 against 0.520) is Vampiric Tutor alone. That is the direction of the trade: from FINDING the piece to drawing more chances at one. deck-audit reads card-advantage at 4 copies against a cited floor of 10 — a floor, not a census: it names nine more cards whose oracle text draws, including Champion of Dusk, Pact of the Serpent, Preacher of the Schism and Voldaren Epicure. Game 001: Champion of Dusk was countered, and the pilot calls it 'the refuel that would have closed the game'.

stages.label: ONE MINT BECOMES EIGHT
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: seven cards that take one token-creation event and multiply it, or add an event of their own. Three are replacement doublers (Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Glory Dominus, Elspeth, Storm Slayer); four make extra tokens (Mavren Fein, Bloodline Keeper, Charismatic Conqueror, Legion's Landing). The brief prices the component at 41.2% of opening sevens, 49.8% by turn three, 73.5% assembled, 62.6% by turn six, mean turn 2.834 — third of the twelve declared targets on assembled rate, behind the castable-Vampire leg (92.3%) and the lord/anthem component (79.0%), and wide enough that this stage carries no single point of failure. Stack 010 is the new fact, and it settles what this model previously could only assert. Elspeth's static ability applies to an eminence token even though Edgar has never entered the battlefield: a replacement effect keys off the EVENT it watches for, not the zone of the ability that causes it. With all three doublers out, ONE eminence trigger creates EIGHT tokens — 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 — and the count is identical under all six application orders, because each doubler gets exactly one opportunity at the event and each multiplies by two. Stack 002 is the two-doubler floor, 1 -> 2 -> 4. Two apologies this stage no longer has to make. Gifted Aetherborn, the {B}{B} cast in stacks 002, 008 and 010, is back in the 99 with this baseline, so those scenarios now show a board this deck can make. And Elspeth's membership in the multiplier group was a name in a file; it is evidence now. What does NOT compound: the tokens are created, not cast, so eminence does not re-trigger on them — the multiplier acts once per cast, and a second cast is a second event.

stages.label: EVERY BODY BILLS EVERY SEAT
stages.what_it_does: Three trigger events, and the declaration now cuts on all three. The kill's leg is six CREATION-keyed payoffs: Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call and Witty Roastmaster deal damage as a creature enters, Corpse Knight causes life loss, Mirkwood Bats fires on the creation itself. At 36.4% of opening sevens, 67.4% assembled, 56.7% by turn six, mean turn 2.954. The two DEATH drains, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, are now a component of their own at 13.7% of openers, 30.4% assembled, 24.1% by turn six — a reachable second line, not the kill's leg. Blood Artist drains 'target player'; Cruel Celebrant reaches each opponent. Stack 011 prices the newest of the six: Mirkwood Bats triggers ONCE PER TOKEN, so N tokens in one event is N triggers and N life per opponent — tracking tokens, never doublers. Two further clocks: Sanctum Seeker per attacking Vampire, Throne of the God-Pharaoh per tapped creature at your end step. Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles any opponent life loss during your turn. Three measurements: stack 009 — one two-mana Vampire, one doubler, three ENTRY payoffs, nine triggers, 12 to each seat, exactly lethal into three seats at 12 with zero margin; stack 008 — five triggers doubled, 10 each; stack 003 — seven Sanctum Seeker triggers doubled to 14 per opponent before blocks. No single point of failure here: 009 kills a three-seat pod with Bloodletter nowhere on the board. Six removal spells live here too, and the baseline cost them breadth. Reading all six, none answers a land: Anguished Unmaking and Stroke of Midnight say nonland, Despark needs mana value 4 or greater, Path to Exile and Winds of Abandon are creature-only, Olivia's Wrath is -X/-X. Generous Gift, 'destroy target permanent', was the card that covered that class.

Mirkwood Bats triggers once per token created, not once per creation event: one doubler, two tokens, 2 life per opponent and 4 across a two-seat pod. The three-doubler figure is stated counterfactually there, because 010's eight-token board holds no Bats and ends with both opponents at 40. Bats is NOT alone in scaling with the doublers — every entry payoff counts the same tokens, so on a doubled eminence event all six of the creation leg fire once per token. What is unique to Bats among the six is the trigger EVENT: it keys on creation rather than on a creature entering, so it also catches Voldaren Epicure's Blood token, and a sweep for 'enters' is exactly how the declaration missed it

stages.label: FIVE CARDS HELD, NOT CAST
stages.what_it_does: The swarm is the deck's whole position, so a sweeper is not a setback but the game. Five cards insure against it: Teferi's Protection, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Deflecting Swat. The brief prices the component at 31.2% of opening sevens, 38.6% by turn three, 61.0% assembled, 49.8% by turn six, mean turn 3.157 — and this is the one component held in hand rather than deployed, so the goldfish figure and the practical figure differ by whatever you were forced to spend that mana on instead. deck-audit reads the protection axis at 7 copies against a 5-7 target and calls it AT, because the taxonomy also counts Mondrak and Purphoros; this model files those two on what they mostly do, in conversion and output. Two of the five are not only insurance. Akroma's Will may choose BOTH modes with a commander on the battlefield — flying, vigilance and double strike alongside protection from each colour — so the save and the kill are one card, and that half is available when Edgar is out (goldfish: cast by turn six in 48.4% of games, mean 6.705, median 6). Deflecting Swat gives target spell or ability new targets, which makes it the only one of the five that answers a targeted counterspell now that Cavern of Souls, whose mana made a Vampire spell uncounterable, has left the baseline; Boros Charm's indestructible mode is not that answer. Game 001 is settled ground and is not re-argued here: the pilot ate three board wipes with none of these five in hand and has ruled that VARIANCE rather than a shortfall — the insurance is in the deck and was not drawn. What the game did show is what this stage is insurance FOR: the low curve put a real board back 'in a turn or two, every time'.

stages.label: TWO ROUTES OUT, AND ONE OF THEM IS ONE CARD
stages.what_it_does: THE COMBAT KILL, ten cards: Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain and Captivating Vampire are lords; Intangible Virtue is new and gives every creature token +1/+1 AND vigilance, so the swarm can attack without giving up its blockers; Shared Animosity gives each attacker +1/+0 for every other attacker sharing its type, which on a typal token board is quadratic; Vampire Socialite, Drana, Indulgent Aristocrat and Knight of the Ebon Legion add counters; Nighthawk Scavenger is a flying deathtouch lifelink body that attacks past a ground stall. The eleventh pump is the commander's own — 'whenever Edgar attacks, put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control' — resolved by checker-passed stack 003 with all seven attackers taking a counter. The declared lord/anthem component is 45.6% of opening sevens, 79.0% assembled, 68.1% by turn six — the highest assembled rate of the eleven declared targets except the castable-Vampire leg itself; note it spans three stages of this model, since it counts Sanctum Seeker (output) and Cordial Vampire (ignition). THE INFINITE: Bloodthirsty Conqueror plus Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose or Sanguine Bond, checker-passed in stacks 004 and 006. Read both on their stated terms — each board holds TWO opponents, and each loop starts from a 3-life gain 'from some source' that no stack verifies, so the seed is a claim. The declaration prices the line at 4.6% assembled, 2.8% by turn six, 10.2% with a tutor, mean turn 5.243, and deck-audit names Conqueror a single point of failure. Game 001 says the same thing from the table: Conqueror was one of the two counterspells that decided it. The stage carries no SPOF, because the combat route at 79.0% assembled needs none of the infinite.

lines.note: Eminence itself costs nothing, so what mana buys here is Edgar's own six-mana body: goldfish casts him by turn six in 48.4% of games, mean 6.705, median 6. The ignition is live without him ever being cast. Game 001's eight-mana cast is settled as piloting, not structure, and is not re-argued.

The one accelerant pointed straight at the trigger: {T}, sacrifice another creature, add {B}{B}{B} 'spend this mana only to cast Vampire, Cleric, and/or Demon spells'. Enumerated over the 99: 28 Vampire creature cards and no non-Vampire Cleric or Demon, so inside this deck the clause is a Vampire-spell restriction — and eminence reads 'whenever you cast ANOTHER Vampire spell', so 27 of those 28 casts fire the trigger and the 28th is Edgar himself, whose cost this mana helps pay while firing nothing. deck-facts flags the same clause as the trap: it cannot pay a coloured activated ability. Unverified as a line.

The refuel exists to put another castable Vampire in hand — that is the whole feedback the engine runs on. Game 001 is the negative case: Champion of Dusk was countered and the pilot calls it 'the refuel that would have closed the game'. No passing stack covers it.

THE ARROW THE OLD MODEL COULD NOT STAMP. Stack 010's scenario names the cast and all three doublers: one {B}{B} Vampire, one eminence trigger, eight tokens (1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8), identical under all six application orders, with Edgar in the command zone having never entered the battlefield.

WITHDRAWN AND REPLACED. The round-1 note routed this arrow through Cordial Vampire and called 002 'a different cast'. Stack 002's scenario.stack[0].object is Gifted Aetherborn — the same card 010 casts — and 002's final_state says in terms 'Cordial Vampire never triggers because nothing dies', so the from-stage card named was the one card in the cited scenario the resolution verifies does NOTHING. The arrow is real and 002 does carry it, through Gifted Aetherborn, which is also in ignition. What 002 adds over 010 is the two-doubler floor: 1 -> 2 -> 4, five new bodies off one {B}{B} cast, and, because 002's board states that an opponent had already lost 3 life this turn, Vampire Socialite's conditional replacement makes the four tokens 2/2s and the cast creature a 3/4.

The primary plan, composing. One {B}{B} Vampire through one doubler (Anointed Procession, in conversion, also on that board) and three ENTRY payoffs: nine triggers, 12 damage to EACH seat, exactly lethal into a three-opponent pod at 12 with zero margin.
Four doubled tokens entering simultaneously are four occurrences, not one: four Purphoros triggers plus a fifth for the cast creature, 5 x 2 = 10 damage to each opponent off one {B}{B} spell.

PROMOTED by stack 011, and re-anchored to do it: the arrow was drawn through Elspeth, whom no stack names beside Bats, and 011 runs it through Anointed Procession instead. One doubler turns one eminence token into two; Mirkwood Bats triggers ONCE PER TOKEN — its trigger event is singular and the one doubled happening contains two occurrences of it — so the tokens drain 2 life from EACH opponent, 4 across 011's two-seat pod. The count follows the tokens in the final modified event, so four tokens is four triggers. Bloodletter of Aclazotz would double the life loss on your turn; no stack tests that and this arrow does not claim it. Re-run mechanically against all NINE presentable passing stacks (002, 003, 004, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011 — 001 and 005 are presentable: false), this is the only dashed line 011 carries: the other ten are still not fully named by any of them, so 8 of 18 is a measured ceiling and not an inherited one. Nearest miss is lines[13], where 004 names Vito and Bloodthirsty Conqueror and misses only Blood Artist — which is that line's own point.

Five new bodies off one {B}{B} cast, and the four tokens each enter with a +1/+1 counter — which needs Socialite out AND an opponent already down life this turn, since her text reads 'AS LONG AS an opponent lost life this turn'. 002 states that condition as a premise of its board. Checker-passed stack 011 is now the other side of it and it is no longer a counterfactual: on a board holding Socialite and Anointed Procession with nothing yet drained, the doubled tokens enter as plain 1/1s, because the life loss they cause has only TRIGGERED as they enter and a replacement effect cannot go back. The delay runs the other way for the spell that caused them — Gifted Aetherborn resolves after both drains and does get the counter, entering as a 3/4. This is the combat kill's input, not a damage claim.
The backward loop: Skullclamp converts a doubled 1/1 into two cards, and Caretaker's Talent draws once per turn on a token entry — so the bodies conversion makes pay for the next cast. Unverified.

Seven Vampire attackers, seven Sanctum Seeker triggers, each doubled by Bloodletter because it is your turn: 14 per opponent at declare-attackers, before blocks. Your 1 life per trigger is NOT doubled.

The same doubling on the end-step clock, and the stack PARTIALLY REFUTES it as a table kill: seven tapped creatures is 14 each, which kills the 9-life seat and leaves the 15-life seat alive at exactly 1. Bloodletter was untapped and did not count itself.

The commander's attack trigger is a permanent, cumulative pump, which stack 003 resolves — but no passing stack names an anthem beside him, so the arrow into the anthems is a claim. This is where Edgar's 48.4%-by-turn-six body is a real cost, unlike at the ignition.

lines.carries: a life swing to seed the loop
lines.note: Stacks 004 and 006 verify the loop from a stated seed and name no seed card, so this is a claim: any drain in the output stage is the life swing the two-card loop needs to start.

Both remaining searches put the card on TOP, not in hand, so each costs a turn — and Forerunner can only find a Vampire, which Conqueror is. The declaration models no tutor; the assisted figures are where they are priced (4.6% assembled against 10.2%).

Stack 004 names the loop's real cost — Conqueror is a creature and every iteration gives an opponent a priority window. Five held cards are the deck's answer; none has been verified doing it, and in game 001 the answer that mattered was a counterspell rather than removal.

via: Legion's Landing // Adanto, the First Fort
lines.note: The feedback loop that makes this an engine rather than a list: Intangible Virtue gives the tokens vigilance, so attacking costs no defence; Legion's Landing transforms when you attack with three or more creatures, tokens included; Mavren Fein mints another token, though only off NONTOKEN Vampires attacking, so the token swarm does not trigger him. Unverified.

The round-2 claim that Skullclamp is 'the deck's cheapest repeatable outlet' is WITHDRAWN — Master of Dark Rites' outlet costs no mana and is mana-POSITIVE ({T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}, spendable on the spells this deck casts). The three at-will outlets are priced, not ranked: Master of Dark Rites is free and tap-gated to once a turn; Skullclamp is {1} per equip at sorcery speed, any number of times, and its +1/-1 kills a 1/1 token as a state-based action while drawing two; Indulgent Aristocrat is {2} a go, also any number of times. All three feed both drains. The tension is Skullclamp's alone and is bigger than round 2 said: its kill needs the token still at 1/1, eight static pumps in the 99 reach a 1/1 Vampire token — two of them at this arrow's own endpoints, Warleader's Call in output and Caretaker's Talent at level 3 in fuel — and Cordial Vampire puts a counter on every Vampire on the FIRST death, so the outlet throttles itself after one kill. The two sacrifice outlets are indifferent to all of it, which is why they are named here. No passing stack covers any of it.

map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn — the eminence trigger every kill proof opens on
map_disagreements.why: The newest declared component is also one of the most scattered, because it is defined by a COST and a TYPE LINE — thirteen Vampires at mana value 2 or less — and the map groups on everything else the card says. Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant file with the drains, Charismatic Conqueror with the token makers, the plain biters with the finishers. So the leg every checker-passed kill proof opens on has three addresses and no name, and Edgar himself is filed in city-2 with the small biters because his printed text reads as a lord. Note the labels quoted here are engine-facts' deterministic fallbacks: deck_map.json was re-laid-out for v1.0.0 and every region's `label` is still null, so deck-cartographer has not named this map.

map_disagreements.component: A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn
map_disagreements.why: The doubling clause is one line on cards whose remaining text is about different things: Mondrak files under Insurance on its indestructible-counter ability, Legion's Landing under Ramp because it flips into a land that taps for {W}. The clause the whole engine multiplies through — the thing stack 010 measures at eight tokens per trigger — is spread across three cities and named by none of them.

map_disagreements.component: A payoff that fires when a token is CREATED (the leg every kill proof uses)
map_disagreements.why: Six cards doing one job at three addresses, and the map's axis is damage versus life loss versus 'indestructible God'. The engine's axis is the trigger EVENT — creation, entry, death — and the DECLARATION now makes that cut, on this model's proposal. The map still does not and structurally cannot: 'this enchantment deals 1 damage to each opponent' and 'each opponent loses 1 life' and 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token' are three sentences a text embedding has no reason to separate, and the separation is a rules fact about when the ability fires. Mirkwood Bats is the proof in both directions: it clusters into city-5 with the drains on its life-loss text, it was the card the old mixed group omitted for keying on 'create' rather than 'enters' — Caretaker's Talent is the near miss, keying on tokens ENTERING, drawing instead of draining, once each turn — and checker-passed stack 011 is what priced it once the cut existed to put it on the right side of.

map_disagreements.component: THE DRAIN DOUBLER (stacks 003/007): Bloodletter of Aclazotz + a drain source
map_disagreements.why: Throne of the God-Pharaoh sits with the bodies because its text counts tapped creatures, while Bloodletter and Sanctum Seeker sit with the drains. Checker-passed stack 007 is precisely the join the map cannot make — and it is also where the join partly fails, killing one seat and leaving another at exactly 1.

Herald's Horn is a typal cost reducer, so its text clusters with the Vampire mass rather than with the rocks — in this engine a discount on the creature you were going to cast anyway is mana, which is why it is filed here against the map. The larger disagreement is not with the map but between two artifacts: Master of Dark Rites is counted by deck-audit's mana-sources axis as a persistent producer and by mana_analysis as one of the 30 black sources, and the goldfish declaration's ramp group does not contain it. The map files it in city-2 with the biters. Three readings, three answers.

Deflecting Swat clusters away from the four saves, because redirecting a spell reads nothing like phasing out your board — and that textual distance is exactly the functional distinction that matters now: after Cavern of Souls left this baseline, Deflecting Swat is the deck's answer to a targeted counterspell, which is the class of card that decided game 001.

unassigned.why: An arrival this baseline that lands in no stage. It is an instant reading 'put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to two target creatures' or 'proliferate' (entwine {3}{W}), it belongs to no declared goldfish component, it appears in no checker-passed stack, and neither mode feeds a conversion this model traces: two counters is small beside Edgar's attack trigger, Cordial Vampire and Vampire Socialite, and the proliferate mode's non-creature target on a typical board is Elspeth's loyalty. Naming it here rather than filing it under the combat kill is the honest reading — the card is a counters-subtheme card in a deck whose counters are incidental.

open_questions.question: Stack 011 settled the round-1 form of this: Mirkwood Bats triggers once per TOKEN, so N tokens created in one event is N triggers and N life per opponent, tracking the tokens and never the doublers. What 011 deliberately left counterfactual is the deck's own board — it holds ONE doubler and two opponents, and 010's eight-token board carries no Bats and ends with both opponents at 40. What does the real go-wide board put on the table: Bats plus two or three doublers into three untouched seats, and does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Bats is the newest payoff and the one the declaration had missed; 011 prices it at 1 life per opponent per token on a one-doubler board, while the conversion stage is measured at three doublers and 011 says putting Bats on that board is a change to it. This is a different board from open_questions[2], which asks the entry payoffs' count from 40 — same missing number, two suites — and between them they are what stands between calling the go-wide payoff a primary clock and calling it a finisher.

open_questions.question: Does Bloodletter of Aclazotz double DAMAGE, not only stated life loss? Its reminder text reads '(Damage causes loss of life.)' and stack 004's checker treated the identical parenthetical on Bloodthirsty Conqueror as reminder text under 207.2a — but stacks 003 and 007 only ever tested 'each opponent loses N life' from Sanctum Seeker and Throne. Nobody has run the other direction: does Purphoros dealing 2 to each opponent become 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether this deck has one kill or two. If damage doubles, the drain doubler and the go-wide payoff class are one engine rather than two plans that happen to share a stage; if it does not, and the map's damage/life-loss split is the correct reading after all.

open_questions.question: How many two-mana Vampire casts does the payoff suite need to take one seat from 40 to 0 with only ONE doubler on the battlefield? Stack 009 is exactly lethal at 12 life per seat and stack 008 measures 10 damage per cast with two doublers.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every verified damage figure in this model starts from a pod already below 15. The thesis calls the go-wide payoff the primary clock; without a count from an untouched table it is only ever proved as a finisher.

open_questions.question: goldfish.py's _TUTOR_RE is the literal phrase 'search your library for a card' and deliberately excludes narrow tutors, so Forerunner of the Legion is not modelled — verified at source, and no longer the question. What is open: should it be, for a deck where 28 of the 99 are the searched type and the tutored card lands on top? And what does THE GO-WIDE KILL's assisted rate become if it is?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The baseline halved the tutor count from four to two and left one of the two Vampire-only, so the 7.5-point assisted gap (0.445 to 0.520) is currently one card's worth. A type-restricted tutor is a wildcard for anything inside its type, and every leg of the go-wide kill except the doublers is inside it — so the exclusion is conservative in general and may be conservative by a lot here. The assisted figures are what prose quotes when it wants to say the deck can find its piece.

open_questions.question: After this baseline the interactive suite covers 3 of 5 classes: deck-audit reads land and graveyard at zero, and reading all six removal spells confirms none answers a land. For a Mardu aggro deck whose pilot logged the whole table making him the archenemy on turn three, is a land answer or graveyard hate load-bearing, or is the correct trade exactly the one made — two premium white removal spells for more cheap Vampire bodies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both departures (Swords to Plowshares, Generous Gift) were efficiency, and both arrivals in their place are engine parts. The engine model can say what the deck no longer answers; it cannot say whether an aggro deck that is already the archenemy should be spending slots on answers at all.

The half that stood is the half the split rests on: a death payoff cannot fire on the creation event stack 009 kills from, and Mirkwood Bats, which does, was in no component at all. Measured effect on disk: THE GO-WIDE KILL 0.491 -> 0.445 assembled, 0.327 -> 0.285 by turn six, mean 4.773 -> 5.043; the creation leg alone is 36.4% of openers, 0.674 assembled, 0.567 by turn six; the death pair 13.7%, 0.304, 0.241. The kill's headline fell 4.2 points because the leg it names got smaller and truer, which is the same shape as the castable-Vampire leg before it.

A primary win line with no target is the defect validate-goldfish-targets was built to catch, and this deck has it for the combat route while it has three legs declared for the go-wide one.

proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Three artifacts disagree about this card. deck-audit counts it under mana-sources as a persistent producer and lists it among the six accelerants; mana_analysis counts it as one of the 30 black sources; the declaration's five-card ramp group does not contain it. Its {B}{B}{B} is restricted to Vampire, Cleric and Demon spells — which is what this deck casts — and it costs a body and a tap, so an exclusion is defensible. What is not defensible is the silence: a reader comparing the ramp component's 60.2% assembled against deck-audit's ramp axis cannot tell that they are counting different sets.

absent_stages.why: STATED, NOT OMITTED, and re-checked against the new list. `fodder` is the resource an engine converts by consuming it, and the two fleet decks that carry the stage populate it with cards whose job is to BE eaten — hapatra's five body-makers, yawgmoth-swarm's eleven bodies-and-recursion. On the same taxonomy edgar-vampires holds TWO sac-outlets (Indulgent Aristocrat's {2}, Sacrifice a creature; Master of Dark Rites' {T}, Sacrifice another creature — the second arrived with this baseline and took the count from one), against seven and nine outlets in those decks, and neither is free or repeatable at will. No CARD in the 99 exists to be consumed, which is the test: the thing this deck eats is tokens, and a token is conversion's output rather than a slot in the 99. Round 1 also said every body is 'then wanted alive', and that is corrected here — Skullclamp wants a 1/1 token dead, for {1}, repeatably, and Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant pay for it. That is a real line and it now carries an arrow (lines[17]); what it is not is a stage, because the eaters are already filed on the jobs they do and the eaten are not cards. The other consumption clauses are costs on cards doing a different job — Mondrak's {1}{W/P}{W/P} activated ability sacrifices two other artifacts and/or creatures for an indestructible counter (which answers destruction only, and a second counter buys nothing, so it cannot be run as a conversion). One taxonomy artifact worth naming: card_roles gives Mirkwood Bats `sac-cost`, matched off the word 'sacrifice' in 'whenever you create or sacrifice a token' — the card has no sacrifice cost at all. Opening a fodder stage would either duplicate the token makers already in ignition and conversion, or file the EATERS under the name of what is eaten.

findings.claim: "Cast the same Vampire on turn two into an untouched table and the four tokens are 1/1s."
findings.note: The only defect I found in round 3, and it is new in round 3 — an illustration attached to a correction that is otherwise exactly right. The board it describes cannot exist on turn two: four tokens off one cast needs BOTH doublers, and Anointed Procession is {3}{W} and Mondrak {2}{W}{W} (cards.json), eight mana of enchantment and creature on a battlefield stack 002 itself gives five lands. The substance is correct and worth keeping — without an opponent already down life the tokens are 1/1s — but the sentence conflates an early CAST with a late BOARD. Two repairs, either fine: drop "on turn two" and let "into an untouched table" carry it, or price the real early case (one doubler, two tokens, no opponent down life, two 1/1s). This needs no critic round: it is an uncapped note field, quotes no figure and cites no stack, so any scoped edit closes it. I record it rather than fail on it — see the verdict note in findings[9].

findings.claim: Round-2 finding 5 fixed at four sites, not the three I named
findings.note: All four now carry the condition, and I checked for a fifth two ways: every leaf string in the artifact containing "Socialite", and every leaf string matching 2/2, 3/4 or "+1/+1 counter" within 200 characters of the word token. Outside `critic` and `rebuttals` there are exactly two claim sites (lines[4], lines[8]) and two evidence sites (stages[3], stages[6]), all conditioned, plus stages[6].what_it_does's "Vampire Socialite, Drana, Indulgent Aristocrat and Knight of the Ebon Legion add counters", which makes no claim about token size and needs none. There is no fifth. The fourth site the engineer found itself — stages[3].evidence[1], on the conversion stage — is a real one I missed, and finding it by grepping every leaf rather than by re-reading the three I was handed is the right method.

findings.where: rebuttals[10] — my proposed replacement superlative, rebutted
findings.claim: "Indulgent Aristocrat reads '{2}, Sacrifice a creature ...' — no tap symbol, so it is repeatable any number of times a turn; only Master of Dark Rites is tap-gated"
findings.note: The rebuttal is correct and my round-2 replacement was wrong. Indulgent Aristocrat's oracle text in cards.json is "Lifelink / {2}, Sacrifice a creature: Put a +1/+1 counter on each Vampire you control" — no {T}, no once-per-turn clause, and no timing restriction, so it is activatable at instant speed as often as mana and creatures allow, where Skullclamp's equip is sorcery-speed. So Skullclamp is not "the only outlet repeatable more than once per turn"; it is not even the more flexible of the two. Pricing all three instead of crowning one is the right answer, and "an enumeration cannot be over-claimed" is the correct principle: I proposed swapping one superlative for another and was caught doing it by the agent I had caught doing it. lines[17] now reads Master free but tap-gated, Skullclamp {1} per equip unlimited, Aristocrat {2} unlimited — each verified against the printed text.

findings.claim: The tension re-sized: eight static pumps reach a 1/1 Vampire token, two at the arrow's own endpoints, plus the Cordial Vampire self-throttle; `via` now names both sacrifice outlets
findings.note: The eight match my enumeration card for card — Intangible Virtue and Caretaker's Talent level 3 (creature tokens), Warleader's Call (creatures you control), Legion Lieutenant, Stromkirk Captain, Captivating Vampire and Lord of Lineage (other Vampires), Patchwork Banner (chosen type) — and the two endpoint cases are right: Warleader's Call is in `output`, the arrow's destination, and Caretaker's Talent in `fuel`, its source. Adding Indulgent Aristocrat and Master of Dark Rites to `via` is the correct response, since a sacrifice kills a 2/2 that the equip cannot. The scope note in rebuttals[11] anticipates the objection I was going to file — that `via` now carries cards from `mana` and `wincon` on a `fuel -> output` arrow — and answers it correctly: validate_engine requires only that each joined stage hold one via card (`via & members`, line 287), Skullclamp is in fuel and both drains in output, and splitting into three arrows would draw one route as three. One compression to watch if this is ever edited again: "the outlet throttles itself after one kill" is true of the tokens already on the battlefield; tokens created after that death are still 1/1s and still clampable, which the round-2 finding said and the round-3 sentence shortens away.

findings.where: lines[0..2], lines[7], lines[9], lines[12..17] — the eleven dashed lines
findings.claim: The orchestrator's question: is 7 of 18 the honest ratio, or could any dashed line be green from a stack that already passes?
findings.note: Answered mechanically, not by judgement. For each of the eleven I tested whether ANY of the eight presentable passing stacks names every one of its `via` cards anywhere in its scenario — stack, hand, graveyard or board. **None does, for any of the eleven.** So not one dashed line could be promoted even under the weakest possible gate, the one that only requires a stack to NAME the cards. The nearest miss is lines[13] (output -> wincon, seeding the infinite): stack 004 names two of its three via cards, Vito and Bloodthirsty Conqueror, and is missing exactly Blood Artist — which is the line's whole point, since 004's seed is "you just gained 3 life (any source)" with no seed card, precisely what the note says. Going the other way, every stage PAIR reachable from a passing stack already carries a green arrow: 002 and 010 give ignition->conversion (lines[3], lines[4]), 008 conversion->output (lines[6]), 009 ignition->output (lines[5]), 002 conversion->wincon (lines[8]), 003 and 007 ignition->output (lines[10], lines[11]). Stacks 004 and 006 hold cards from `wincon` and nothing else, so they can only ever be stage evidence and never an arrow — and that is exactly how the wincon stage uses them. All eight presentable stacks are cited; 001 and 005, the non-presentable pair, are cited nowhere. 7 of 18 is not merely honest, it is maximal: it is every arrow the current evidence can carry.

It matches my independent measurement in every particular, and I re-checked the two totals now written into the module docstring: nine tracked engine.json hold 120 lines of which 57 carry a verified_by (18/10/15/18/13/9/11/11/15 and 7/4/10/3/4/9/3/6/11). The docstring's diagnosis is the part worth having and it is stated correctly: edgar's defect and ur-dragon's correct line are structurally identical — a `from` stage holding the cast on the stack and the converter on the battlefield, `via` naming the converter — and the discriminator is a rules fact (Cordial Vampire never triggers because nothing dies) that no shape test can see. I am satisfied with it as written, including the decision NOT to withdraw the `carries` reasoning: that is a second and independent reason the as-worded version fails, since `carries` is prose the engineer writes and a rename evades the check silently. My round-1 note said a finding of this kind should become a mechanical check; the corrected answer, measured three times, is that this one should not, and the measurement is now somewhere the next person to have the idea will meet it.

findings.where: lines[3], lines[5], lines[6], lines[8], lines[10], lines[11], lines[4]
findings.claim: The seven verified lines, on a third reading
findings.note: Re-confirmed rather than assumed. lines[4] is the one that was repaired: 002's stack[0].object is the Gifted Aetherborn cast, both doublers are on the battlefield, final_state gives 1 -> 2 -> 4 and new_bodies 5, and every card in `via` is one the resolution shows acting — the arrow is carried, and the floor/ceiling pair with 010 is worth more than dropping the line would have been. The other six are unchanged from round 1 and I have now read each against its stack three times: 010 (eight tokens, order-independent, Edgar never on the battlefield), 009 (nine triggers, 12 per seat, exactly lethal at 12 with zero margin), 008 (five triggers doubled, 10 each), 002 (five bodies, now correctly conditioned), 003 (seven triggers doubled to 14, your gain not doubled), 007 (partially refuted as a table kill, and cited for the refutation).

Stating the reasoning so it can be overruled. The round-2 fail rested on two things — a false superlative on a new arrow, and a conditional replacement effect asserted unconditionally on two solid-green lines. Both are fixed, one of them more thoroughly than I asked. Against the charter's three fail triggers: no line asserts a flow its cited stack does not establish (all seven re-read); no figure is wrong (every quoted rate re-derived from goldfish_metrics.json and engine-facts --json); no dashed line is written as fact, and the dashed set is now provably maximal rather than merely honest. What remains is findings[0] — one illustrative clause describing a board that cannot exist on turn two. It quotes no measurement, cites no stack, carries no badge and sits in an uncapped field. Failing a terminal round on it would ship an artifact labelled "could not be grounded" for the most thoroughly grounded engine model I have read, and the label would be false. If the orchestrator would rather not ship a `pass` carrying a non-`supported` finding, the honest route is a scoped edit to that one clause rather than a fourth round: nothing else in the artifact depends on it.

rebuttals.finding: round 2 · critic.findings[1] and findings[2] — the structural variant, 'over-claimed' and 'unjustified' as a permanent check
rebuttals.response: accepted on the fleet measurement; the round-2 reasoning stands and is not withdrawn
rebuttals.what_i_did: Re-ran both formulations over all nine tracked engine.json and their passing stacks rather than reading the critic's numbers back, and I reproduce them. THE RECORD, in the form this repo keeps its rejected checks. PROPOSED: for each cited scenario extract the cards named in scenario.stack[] with build_index.line_cards; if they all belong to one stage, that stage is the scenario's ACTING stage, and any line whose `from` is that acting stage must have `via` ∩ `from` intersect the stack[] set. MEASURED against the fleet as tracked today (57 verified lines across nine decks): the AS-WORDED version — a via card from the from-stage must simply appear in stack[] — fires 46 times, including 9 of radagast's 9 on a critic-passed artifact, so it is dead on arrival. THE VARIANT fires ONCE, on ur-dragon lines[3], and that one is a FALSE POSITIVE: `conversion -> output` via [Miirym, Sentinel Wyrm, Terror of the Peaks] citing stack 002, whose stack[0].object is Lathliss, Dragon Queen — which ur-dragon also files in `conversion` — so via ∩ from = {Miirym} misses {Lathliss}, while 002's resolution is Miirym's trigger doubling under Panharmonicon, exactly what the arrow says. Add edgar's round-1 artifact and it fires twice: that false positive plus lines[4], the true defect. Precision 1 in 2. So: NOT AN ERROR CHECK, on the same rule that rejected three checks in validate_goldfish_targets — a validator that fires on correct data trains its reader to ignore it.
rebuttals.where_i_disagree: Nothing on the verdict, and I am not withdrawing the round-2 reasoning that got here, because it is the half that generalises. WHY IT CANNOT BE REPAIRED, which is the part worth keeping: edgar's defect and ur-dragon's correct line are structurally IDENTICAL — a line whose `from` stage holds two cards, one on the stack and one on the battlefield, with `via` naming the battlefield one. In ur-dragon that card is doing the work; in edgar round 1 it was doing nothing (002: 'Cordial Vampire never triggers because nothing dies'). The discriminator is whether that card's ability fires in the resolution, which is a rules fact and not a shape, and the only textual tell is that 002 names the card solely in the negative — i.e. negation detection, the string matching validate_engine's docstring says the same wrong line survives a rephrase of. The as-worded version had to be rejected for a second and separate reason that still holds: it can only be made precise by keying on `carries`, which is free prose the engineer writes, so renaming 'token-creation events' to 'bodies' evades it silently. IF IT IS WANTED AT ALL, ship it report-only: two lines across nine decks is cheap for a human to read and a false error is not.
